correctness.rationale: The graph metric gives three entry values 1,x,x⁴. The DFT of the rim and the two-dimensional hub-constant sector is a complete orthogonal block diagonalization. Min eigenvalue f_n, hub determinant g_n, strict root uniqueness, rational 4–8 versus 9+ comparison and endpoint multiplicities were proved. The implicit-function expansion at n^-1/2 gives the logarithmic limit. Direct matrices and rational tests passed, with no inference of infinite proof from finite samples.

originality.rationale: Bounded statement-level comparison found no earlier exact classification for exp(-t d²) on all wheel orders, no order-nine swap, and no growing half-logarithmic critical bandwidth. Closest wheel-specific papers treat negative type of unsquared distance, and geodesic-kernel general results need different hypotheses. Genuine residual risk of a differently named general finite-matrix theorem remains.
residual_risks: A general circulant-plus-rank-one positive matrix classification could already give the wheel threshold as an unlabelled corollary.
The 2020 wheel-distance inverse paper was available only at abstract/introduction scope; its full content was not used for a whole-document negative conclusion.
The result is a specialized exact graph family and not a classification of all diameter-two graphs.

value.rationale: Graph-geodesic Gaussian covariance validity is a natural kernel/interpolation question. The exact sharp admissible ray for every wheel, non-obvious hub-versus-rim obstruction switch at nine rim vertices, critical nullities and logarithmic growth of the bandwidth threshold are mathematically specific, not a trivial finite example, and explain how one hub forces increasingly narrow correlations in large cyclic samples.
